subject: Operational accountability pledge & verification for Kestrel surge
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@kestrelretail.com>, Anya Patel <anya.patel@kestrelretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operational accountability pledge & verification for Kestrel surge

Team,

Quick recap: on 2028-06-14 (20:50 UTC) Kestrel saw a sustained throughput collapse and 95th/99th tail latency spike during a checkout campaign window. Carlos flagged the impact to their payments flows and requested an exec-level assurance and remediation plan.

Attached is an initial RCA draft and a mitigation checklist (kestrel_rca_v1.pdf, mitigation-checklist.xlsx). I need a tight ownership and verification plan so we can (1) present commitments to Kestrel tomorrow and (2) prove closure to our execs by EOW.

Please confirm the following by EOD today:
- Primary owners for each corrective action in the attached checklist
- Short verification steps (what evidence we'll hand to Kestrel)
- Expected ETA per item (date and time where possible)

I'll consolidate and produce a one-page exec readout. Rishi — can you surface the kernel/serving changes that reduced throughput? Monica — please lead rollback and hotfix coordination. Grace — recommend verification criteria and evidence collection (logs, traces, synthetic runs).

Kimberly
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kestrel_rca_v1.pdf (pdf), mitigation-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Rivera <c.rivera@kestrelretail.com>, Anya Patel <anya.patel@kestrelretail.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational accountability pledge & verification for Kestrel surge

Kimberly — ack. Short answers below:

Root cause summary (short): an aggressive kernel-chooser path selected a quantized execution variant that deoptimized KV cache eviction under the workload distribution Kestrel produced (many short-lived sessions + long tail sequences from retries). That increased token emission latency and backpressured batching, collapsing throughput.

Owners & ETAs (initial):
- Action A: Pin kernel selector to prior stable policy for Kestrel pool — owner: Rishi Malhotra — ETA: 2028-06-15T15:00-07:00
- Action B: Patch KV cache eviction threshold to account for short session churn — owner: Monica Patel — ETA: 2028-06-16T12:00-07:00
- Action C: Synthetic replay and SLA test harness run (pre/post) — owner: Grace Oconnor — ETA: 2028-06-16T18:00-07:00

Evidence we'll provide:
- Pre/post latency graphs (95/99), request/second traces, kernel selection logs (kdrive id), and a short video of the synthetic run console.

I'll attach a short kernel-change diff to the RCA link. Will update JIRA KST-4921 after Action A lands.

Rishi
Sr. Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: 2028-06-17T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational accountability pledge & verification for Kestrel surge — verification results

Quick verification summary:
- Action A (kernel pin) applied 2028-06-15T15:05-07:00 — immediate 40% throughput bump observed in the Kestrel pool; 95p latency improved from 420ms -> 120ms within 10 minutes.
- Action B (KV eviction threshold patch) applied 2028-06-16T11:50-07:00; after warmup, sustained error rate dropped below 0.18% for a 90-minute window during synthetic and customer traffic.

Evidence attached: latency-graphs.png (pre/post), and the synthetic run logs (linked in Drive). I've uploaded the verification checklist and a short video clip to the drive link in related_links.

Next steps I recommend:
- Formalize a post-incident test schedule (24/72/168 hour checks) for Kestrel's pool for the next 7 days — owner: Monica
- Ship RCA v1 to Kestrel execs with the evidence bundle — owner: Kimberly (by 2028-06-18 09:00-07:00)
- Postmortem deep-dive (serving runtime) in 2 weeks to discuss a longer-term kernel-selector guardrail — owner: Rishi

Grace
Principal Reliability Engineer
